column3: A pier that reaches about 440 meters out into Qingdao Bay, with a small pavilion at its end, and a symbol of the city.
A museum in the old brewery founded in 1903, which shows how beer is made and lets you taste it fresh.
A coastal mountain where cliffs meet the sea, with Taoist temples and springs, known for its clear spring water.
A leafy district of villas in many European styles, along quiet, tree-lined streets near the sea.
A twin-spired Catholic church from the German era in Qingdao, a Gothic-style landmark on a hill.
A seafront square with a big red sculpture called May Wind, with Olympic sailing nearby.
A small island with a white lighthouse, connected by a path, and a quiet, pretty spot by the bay.
A long beach of fine golden sand on the east coast of Qingdao, a place for swimming and festivals.
China's best-known beer, born in Qingdao, and in summer you can even drink it fresh from a plastic bag.
Clams, shrimp, crab and fish from the Yellow Sea are fresh and simply cooked in Qingdao's restaurants.
A beachside favorite of clams stir-fried in chili and garlic, which goes very well with cold beer.
Dumplings filled with Spanish mackerel and chives, a Shandong coastal specialty, with a fresh, sweet flavor.
Every summer, Qingdao holds a beer festival with huge tents, live music and thousands of visitors.
A spring that bubbles up from the ground in three jets, the most famous of Jinan's many springs, which is why Jinan is called the City of Springs.
A lake in the city center with lotus flowers, willows and old pavilions, fed by the springs of Jinan.
A hill with Buddhist carvings above the city of Jinan, with a temple and a view over the city.
A spring that gushes through stone tiger heads into a moat, where locals come to fill their bottles with spring water.
A street of snacks near the springs, with old shops and stalls, where you can try local treats such as fried milk.
An old temple south of Jinan, with a forest of pagodas and rare Song-dynasty statues of monks.
Pork intestine braised in a sweet-sour sauce, repeated several times, a Shandong classic with a rich flavor.
Braised pork served over rice, a simple and filling local meal in Jinan.
A flaky, layered bread with scallion, rolled in a spiral and baked until golden.
A savory millet porridge with peanuts, vermicelli and vegetables, a traditional breakfast in Jinan.
The local opera of Shandong, with simple tunes and stories about village life.
A vast temple complex for Confucius in his hometown, with many halls and ancient cypress trees. It is part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The mansion of the Confucius family, with over 400 rooms, where the descendants of Confucius lived for centuries.
A large forest cemetery for Confucius and his descendants, with thousands of stone steles and old trees.
A banquet cuisine of the Confucius family, with elegant dishes that were served to officials and emperors.
A crisp sesame flatbread from Qufu, baked in a clay oven and eaten fresh.
A ceremony in Qufu to honor Confucius with music, dance and offerings, held every year in autumn.
The teaching system that grew from Confucius's ideas of virtue, learning and family, which shaped China and East Asia.
The most honored of the Five Sacred Mountains. Emperors made offerings here, and pilgrims climb 6,000 stone steps to see the sunrise from the top. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
A temple at the foot of Mount Tai where emperors made offerings, with big halls and old cypresses.
The highest point of Mount Tai, with a small temple and a view of the clouds.
A feast made from tofu in many forms, with water from the mountain springs.
A fish from the cold streams of Mount Tai, steamed or fried, with sweet and tender meat.
A cliff pavilion in Penglai, linked to the legend of the Eight Immortals crossing the sea, and said to show visions of mirages.
Sweet, crisp red apples from the orchards of Yantai, one of the best-known apple regions in China.
Sea cucumber from the cold Bohai Sea is a highly valued seafood, cooked in rich sauces.
Hand-pulled noodles from Fushan, served with a rich meat topping, a famous Yantai dish.
Changyu is one of China's oldest wine brands, founded in 1892 in Yantai, with a wine museum in an old cellar.
Sea cucumber from the clean waters of Weihai, a prized local seafood, usually braised or in soup.
A common street snack of squid grilled on a stick, brushed with a spicy sauce.
A museum of Weifang's kites, a craft that has been practiced for centuries, in the city that hosts a kite festival.
A pot of pork and offal stewed all day, served with flatbread, a Weifang tradition.
A crisp, juicy radish that is eaten like a fruit, a Weifang specialty.
Grilled meat that you wrap in small flatbreads with scallions and a sauce, which became a viral hit in 2023.
A thin, crisp sesame flatbread from Zhoucun, so thin that it breaks at a touch.
Colored glass art made in Boshan, where craftsmen have made glass for centuries, in bright colors.
A temple to Mencius, the second sage of Confucianism, in his hometown Zoucheng.
A fried chicken dish tossed with dried chilies, a local favorite in Jining.
A hill area of Shandong with a revolutionary history, with villages that supported the army in the 1940s.
A thin, crepe-like bread cooked on a griddle, and rolled with scallions and sauce, a Shandong staple.
Chicken stir-fried with spices and served in a pot, a Linyi favorite.
A green tea grown in the north, where cool weather and sea air give it a strong, fresh flavor.
Fresh catches from the Yellow Sea, served simply by the shore.
The place where the Yellow River reaches the sea, with a wide delta of wetlands and many migratory birds.
Crabs from the Yellow River delta, in autumn, with rich, creamy roe.
A famous braised chicken, cooked so long that the meat falls off the bone. Its shape, with the legs crossed, is easy to spot.
A layered, baked flatbread that is often filled with meat or eaten on its own, a Liaocheng specialty.
A rural mansion of the late Qing, with walled courtyards and halls, the home of a wealthy local family.
A pot dish of meat and vegetables simmered at the table, a tradition for family gatherings.
A spicy fried chicken dish, with chilies and a lot of garlic, a Zaozhuang favorite.
Heze is the main place in China that grows peonies, with huge fields blooming in spring.
A white, milky lamb soup that is simmered for hours, popular for breakfast in Shanxian.
Laiwu's ginger is famous for its large, juicy roots and strong aroma.
